Where it began

Matthew Hayden was born in Kingaroy, Queensland, on 29 October 1971, and went to school at Marist College Ashgrove. He played his state cricket for Queensland, and over 101 Sheffield Shield matches he scored 8,831 runs for them at 54.85.

His first Test came at Johannesburg in March 1994, when he stood in for Mark Taylor against South Africa. A maiden Test hundred followed against the West Indies at Adelaide in 1996-97.

The player

He played 103 Tests for Australia between 1994 and 2009, scoring 8,626 runs at 50.74 with 30 hundreds and 29 fifties, and as a fine slip fielder he held 128 catches. With Justin Langer he opened in more than 100 Test innings, and together they put on 5,654 runs.

The turning point was the tour of India in 2001, where he made 549 runs in three Tests, an Australian record for a series that long. After that he was a fixture. He passed 1,000 Test runs in a calendar year in five years running, the first man to do it five times. At the WACA in October 2003 he made 380 against Zimbabwe, a new world record for a Test innings. Brian Lara took it back six months later, but by 2024 no Australian had made more.

What made him special

He was a powerful, attacking left-hander who liked to take the game to the bowlers from the first over. In one-day cricket he was just as fierce: at the 2007 World Cup he made 659 runs, including a hundred off 66 balls against South Africa, and he won World Cups in 2003 and 2007.

Patience was needed early on, mostly from him. Before that India tour he averaged 24.36 from 13 Tests, and he spent long seasons piling up runs for Queensland while he waited. The wait was rather worth it.

Away from the middle

He is a keen cook who would feed his team-mates on tour, and he published The Matthew Hayden Cookbook in 2004 and a second volume in 2006. He was named a Wisden Cricketer of the Year in 2003, received the Australian Sports Medal, and was made a Member of the Order of Australia in 2010. He entered the Australian Cricket Hall of Fame in 2017.

He won the IPL Orange Cap with Chennai Super Kings in 2009, took on the role of ambassador to the Australian Indigenous Education Foundation, and later commentated and coached, helping Pakistan at the 2021 and 2022 T20 World Cups.

And finally

After that 66-ball hundred against South Africa, St Kitts and Nevis made him an honorary citizen. Few batsmen have been made citizens of another country on the strength of a single innings.
